cards.claim: Any J = M⁻¹K with K antisymmetric satisfies JᵀM + MJ = 0
cards.figure: The tangent to every orbit is J·x; the group it generates preserves Q.

cards.claim: Elliptic case (det M > 0): A(s) = cos s·I + sin s·J has AᵀMA = M
cards.figure: Orbits are the ellipses Q = const, closing after s = 2π; in 3D they are horizontal rings on the bowl z = Q.

check.verifier: sympy.simplify, symbolic a, b, e with det M = e² > 0

cards.claim: Hyperbolic case (det M < 0): A(s) = cosh s·I + sinh s·J has AᵀMA = M
cards.figure: Orbits are hyperbola branches Q = const on the saddle z = Q; they never close.

check.verifier: sympy.simplify, symbolic a, b, e with det M = −e² < 0

cards.claim: Null vectors are η-orthogonal to themselves: (1,1)ᵀη(1,1) = 0
cards.figure: On the saddle, the null lines sit at height 0 — a vector lying on its own orthogonal line.

cards.claim: Residual of the G-projection is G-orthogonal: uᵀG(v − (uᵀGv / uᵀGu)u) = 0
cards.figure: The drop line from v to the u-axis lands in the G-orthogonal plane, not the visually perpendicular one.

cards.claim: ∇(xᵀGx) = 2Gx, so the tangent plane of the unit ball at û has normal Gu
cards.figure: The G-orthogonal plane of u is drawn parallel to the ellipsoid's tangent plane where u pierces it.

cards.claim: Over one period [0, 2π], {cos kt, sin kt}ₖ₌₁³ has Gram matrix π·I
cards.figure: The Gram heatmap shows a clean diagonal at L = T; off-diagonal cells light up as L drifts from T.

cards.claim: Closed form used live: ∫₀ᴸ cos t·cos 3t dt = ½(sin 2L/2 + sin 4L/4)
cards.figure: Each Gram cell in the app is this formula, not a numerical approximation.

cards.claim: Parseval for a 3-harmonic trig sum: ∫₀^{2π} x² dt = π Σ(aₖ² + bₖ²)
cards.figure: The time-domain energy bar and the coefficient-sphere radius² are the same number.

cards.claim: On any interval: ‖x₁+x₂‖² = ‖x₁‖² + ‖x₂‖² + 2⟨x₁,x₂⟩; the cross term is 0 at L = 2π
cards.figure: The parallelepiped of parts is square-cornered exactly when the cross terms vanish.

cards.claim: Time-average ⟨cos(ωt+φ), cos(ω(t+τ)+φ)⟩ = ½cos ωτ, independent of φ
cards.figure: The defect landscape is computed from amplitudes only; changing phases leaves it unchanged.

cards.claim: [added after B5a FAILED] time-average ⟨cos(ωt+φ), cos(ω(t+τ)+φ)⟩ = ½cos ωτ, independent of φ
cards.figure: The defect landscape is computed from amplitudes only; changing phases leaves it unchanged.

check.verifier: product-to-sum identity + bound |∫osc| ≤ 1/ω, then limit T → ∞

cards.figure: The defect curve is the autocorrelation curve flipped: valleys of D are peaks of ρ.

cards.claim: r = p/q ⇒ D(2πq) = 0 exactly (a true symmetry of the shifted signal)
cards.figure: Rational ridges of the landscape touch zero at τ = 2πq; irrational ones never do.

cards.claim: The 24 signed permutation matrices with det +1 form a group (closed under products)
cards.figure: Every animated rotation in the panel is one of these 24, played as a turn about its axis.
Dragging the point onto a symmetry axis merges orbit points and grows the stabilizer.

cards.claim: The cyclic shift (x₁,x₂,x₃) ↦ (x₃,x₁,x₂) equals the 120° rotation about (1,1,1)
cards.figure: Shifting the signal is drawn as turning the point about the diagonal; the orbit is an equilateral triangle.

cards.claim: P = (I + S + S²)/3 is the orthogonal projector onto span(1,1,1): P² = P, Pᵀ = P
cards.figure: The orbit's centroid sits on the diagonal; the residual lies in the plane x₁+x₂+x₃ = 0.
